reference_audio.note: The engine transcribes the reference clip with Whisper (openai/whisper-base on GPU, whisper-tiny on CPU) — there is no transcript field, and every request pays the ASR cost.  Only the first prompt_duration seconds are used; roughly 10 s of clean speech clones best.  The first request after startup also pays a one-time librosa initialisation (~10 s).

parameters.name: audio_base64
parameters.description: Reference voice sample (roughly 10 s works well) as a base64 string.  Any container soundfile can decode (WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC, ...).  The engine transcribes it with Whisper for conditioning (there is no transcript field); only its first prompt_duration seconds are used.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Two-letter language code, e.g. 'en' or 'zh'.  Accepted for API consistency but not forwarded — the engine has no language parameter; its tokenizer auto-detects English and Chinese per text segment (other scripts are dropped).  Omitted or empty defaults to 'en'.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random seed for reproducibility.  If omitted, a random seed in [1, 1000] is chosen and echoed in the response.

parameters.name: num_steps
parameters.description: Flow-matching sampling steps.  The model is distilled for 4 (README: 3-4 is best for efficiency); higher is slower with diminishing quality.

parameters.name: t_shift
parameters.description: Flow-matching time shift (README: higher can sound better but with worse word error rate).

parameters.name: return_smooth
parameters.description: Use the 24 kHz vocoder head (upsampled to 48 kHz) instead of the full-band 48 kHz head.  Try this if you hear metallic artifacts (README).

parameters.name: prompt_duration
parameters.description: Seconds of the reference clip to use for conditioning (README: lower can speed up inference; 1000 if you find artifacts).

parameters.name: prompt_rms
parameters.description: Target RMS for the reference clip (README: higher makes it sound louder, ~0.01 recommended; engine default 0.001).
